text:
marta: quick thread — when onboarding customers into Private, what's our recommended pattern to preserve customer egress IP without doing manual peering for every tenant? considering a lightweight relay (managed by us, SNAT per-tenant) vs full per-customer VPC peering. want tradeoffs: ops, security, cost, and a small rollout plan. cc @sam @jia

sam: relay is faster to onboard, lower ops overhead initially, avoids cross-account peering approvals. tradeoffs: extra network hop, connection tracking state, and we become responsible for egress IP reputation.

jia: peering gives best isolation and audit trail (vpc flow logs inside customer account), but onboarding time + route table churn + IAM approvals are slower. long-term ops higher but security posture simpler.

leo: can we do a hybrid? use relay for sandbox/dev/devops customers and auto-escalate to peering for enterprises that need SOC2/SLA. automate peering with terraform to reduce manual work.

tom: security notes — peering reduces our control-plane surface but increases blast radius if route filters are misconfigured. relay requires strict ACLs on the relay instance, per-tenant SNAT mapping, and end-to-end auditing. need to check KMS/access patterns too.

ops-bot: ticket created: ENGNET-1423 "evaluate relay SNAT pool autoscale and audit requirements"

marta: sketch of what I mean for relay mapping:
```yaml
customer_subnet: 10.12.0.0/24
relay_eni: eni-relay-01
snat_map: 10.12.0.0/24 -> 54.23.12.45
lease_ttl: 6h
```
Is that close to what we'd implement?

jia: yes, that's the idea. add ephemeral lease rotation (6h or on reconnect) and log each lease assignment to audit logs. also track egress IP usage per tenant.

sam: quick cost sketch: relay NAT instances + bandwidth is recurring. rough ballpark: for small customers (<100 rps) relay cost < manual peering time + infra. for high-throughput tenants peering is cheaper at scale. I'll post a more detailed model.

leo: operational question — static routes or BGP for the relay handoff? static is simpler for onboarding but BGP will give better HA for larger customers. propose default static, opt-in BGP for enterprise.

tom: ops checklist item: tune conntrack and ephemeral port limits on relay nodes. iptables/conntrack defaults will blow up at scale.

marta: next steps proposal:
1) spike: provision relay for 2 sandbox customers (no SLA)
2) measure p95 latency, conntrack, cost per 100k requests
3) document compliance checklist for SOC2/enterprise tenants and decide escalation criteria to peering
4) draft runbook and automation for peering (terraform + PR template)

jia: add metrics to the spike: egress IP churn, SNAT pool exhaustion, conntrack counts, failed outbound TCP resets, cost per GB.

sam: I'll do the cost model and post numbers in this thread by EOD Friday.

marta: :thumbsup: I'll schedule the spike and create the runbook template.

deploybot: draft RFC created at rfc/relay-onboarding-spike.md (WIP)

ops-bot: reminder — include iptables conntrack tuning and observability (conntrack, netstat) in the spike checklist.

marta: thanks all — lets sync in engineering sync after initial measurements.
